name: IEC polarity indicator at input (active-low input)
summary: Small triangle on an input lead meaning a low level produces the internal active state.
description: The polarity indicator is a small right-angled triangle drawn on the input line where it meets the outline. It states that the L level produces the internal 1 state. Because it refers directly to levels, it does not need a positive or negative logic declaration, which is why device data books favour it.

On drawings that combine device-level schematics with functional logic, the polarity triangle tells the reader that a pin is active low, such as an enable, chip-select or reset input. In positive logic it means the same as a negation circle.
The triangle does not indicate an internal pull-up or default state for an unconnected input. Those details are device data.
readingNotes: Read the triangle as active when low.
Equivalent to a negation circle only in positive logic.
drawingChecklist: Draw the triangle on the outside of the outline, pointing in the signal direction.
Use it consistently in place of circles on level-based schematics.
Name active-low nets with a consistent suffix or overbar.
distinction: The negation circle is a logic statement that needs a declared convention; the triangle is a level statement.
